title: High accuracy can still miss the minority class
description: Course activity for Exercise 10: on a fixed 90 percent control / 10 percent autism cohort, compare ordinary logistic regression against logistic regression with class_weight="balanced" at any chosen classification threshold, using fixed test-set predicted probabilities.
instructions: Choose ordinary or class-weighted logistic regression and a classification threshold. The confusion matrix and metrics below recompute from fixed predicted probabilities on the same locked test participants -- the model is never refit.
reflectionPrompts: Which model detects more autistic participants at the threshold you chose?
Which model looks better if you inspect accuracy alone?
Is 94% accuracy useful when the majority baseline is 90%?
Which kind of error -- a missed autism case, or a false alarm -- matters more for the intended application?
